judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Payable only as interest with respect to such Loan is received by the Company' is compressed and the accrual/waiver sentence adds further complexity, though the rate is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It treats components paid directly to the Servicer as the Servicer's property, which must be squared with 5.4's framing of these as fees the Company pays the Manager and with 5.3(f)'s aggregate cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise percentage of late charges; the defined label 'Default Fee Percentage' is a misnomer for an amount but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The label is used in 5.3(f)'s compensation cap consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The regular state interest rate payable to the Company' appears to be a typo for 'stated' rate, and the phrase as written has no clear referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Default Interest' is used in 5.3(f)'s cap, so the drafting slip carries into that limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short enumeration of fee types payable to the Manager as received by the Company; the defined term is misspelled but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.6 and 5.7(a) provide that brokerage/origination fees received directly by the Manager remain the Manager's property with no Company interest, which overlaps awkwardly with this clause's assumption that such fees are paid to the Company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite fee category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Referenced consistently in 5.3(f)'s cap on Loan Services compensation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All costs, fees, and expenses ... in connection with the formation, organization, reorganization, operation and general administration' plus 'including without limitation' and 'any extraordinary expenses' is a general catch-all of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusion of Loan Services expenses must be read with 5.3(f) and 5.4(b), and the reference to indemnification 'pursuant to the Operating Agreement' imports terms outside this instrument (cf. 5.5(c)).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The foregoing expenses and indemnifications' refers to indemnifications that are not described until 5.5(c), a defective backward reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Permitted Expenses' is defined here but appears nowhere else in the Agreement, leaving the definition orphaned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The class indemnified is 'members, officers, employees, and consultants of the Company' yet the carve-out is framed by reference to 'the Manager's duties under the operating agreement', a mismatch that muddies who loses the benefit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Indemnification expenses are folded into Company Expenses by 5.5(a) via the Operating Agreement, and 4.3 disclaims Manager fiduciary duties, so the scope of protected conduct is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sprawling sentence with 'or similar compensation' and multiple parentheticals; the reach of the general words against the enumerated categories is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It allocates to the Manager fees that 5.4(e) and 5.7(a) treat as flowing through the Company, requiring reconciliation of who owns which fee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For which it will receive a brokerage, origination, renewal or forbearance fees from the borrower' has an ambiguous antecedent for 'it' and a number disagreement, and the fee is set 'on a case-by-case basis'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.7(c) imposes conditions on the same purchases of loans from affiliates, and 5.6 states the Loan Origination Fee remains the Manager's property, so this permission must be harmonised with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) requires a price simultaneously 'no higher than the independently appraised value' and 'no lower than' the Company's investment, a pair of limits that may be impossible to satisfy, and the sub-numbering repeats (i)/(ii) confusingly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (iv) then disapplies the whole protective regime for Sponsored Investment Funds and Private Clients, whose definitions in 5.1(b)-(c) are very wide, largely undoing the protection; 5.3(d) also grants unqualified sale discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The borrower shall not be default under the loan' is ungrammatical, and 'the loan underwriting criteria customarily applied by the Company' is a vague standard with no external referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It regulates purchases from Sponsored Investment Funds and Private Clients whose defined scope (5.1(b)-(c)) determines its bite, and it must be reconciled with 5.3(e)'s unqualified 'sole discretion' power to purchase Portfolio Loans from the same persons.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fair market value of such loan, whichever is greater' is a determinable but contestable measure, and the closing sentence's exception cross-refers to 5.7(e)(iii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3(e) authorises the same sales 'in the Manager's sole discretion', so the pricing floor here has to be read as the controlling specific provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition turns on whether 'the borrower is an Affiliate', then a closing paragraph excludes loans where the borrower is a Sponsored Investment Fund or Private Client — a general prohibition against enumerated carve-outs whose combined effect is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 5.1(a)'s Affiliate definition and 5.1(c)'s Sponsored Investment Fund definition (which names R.E. Loans, LLC), the carve-out can swallow the 20% cap in (ii) and the Manager repurchase duty in (iii), an incoherence with the protective purpose of Article 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terms no less favorable to the Company than terms negotiated in an arm's length transaction' is a familiar but imprecise benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The subordination ordering (behind Company Borrowings and the Lien) is consistent with 2.3(b) and 5.3(a), so no conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No less advantageous to the Company than ... an arm's length transaction ... in the same geographical market with comparable property as security' is a comparative standard whose application is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to 5.7 for Noteholders who are also Manager or Servicer Affiliates, while 5.1(a) expressly excludes Noteholders from the Affiliate definition, producing a circularity that must be untangled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad outside-activities waiver ending with 'no provision of this Agreement shall be deemed to prohibit any such person from conducting such other businesses or activities'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That sweeping saving clause is in tension with the specific prohibitions and conditions in 5.7(b)-(e) and 6.2, which do constrain Manager and affiliate conduct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Noteholders holding a majority of the aggregate principal amounts of Notes' is workable but not the defined 'Majority in Interest'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.2 defines 'Majority in Interest' as exceeding fifty percent and 6.1 states its own trigger, so three overlapping formulations of the same consent threshold coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short lead-in with a definite trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the Section 6 chapeau's condition but omits the majority-consent override stated there, a duplication that may be read as inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Promptly upon the issuance of the Notes' is a definite, if soft, timing obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the Security Agreement of 2.3(a), whose priority is qualified by 5.3(a); perfection and subordination are compatible but pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear ratable-payment covenant, expressly subject to the prepayment discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for 1.4 (including 1.4(b)'s selective prepayment of ERISA and regulatory Noteholders) substantially qualifies the ratability promise and 1.4(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such amount of their business time ... as is reasonably necessary to effectively manage the affairs' is a vague standard with no measurable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.9 expressly permits the Manager's principals to pursue outside businesses, which sits against this time-commitment covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any reasonable time during normal business hours after reasonable advance notice' is standard; the GAAP/IFRS election is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Inspection rights are extended to 'Members and Noteholders' although 4.3 states Purchasers do not become members, a coherent but loosely drafted overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b) makes the reports 'such ... as the Company, in its discretion, may determine', which largely empties the covenant of content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 1.2(a) similarly leaves posting of Loan Amount information to the Company's sole discretion, so the reporting scheme is consistently discretionary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercially reasonable efforts to prevent the structure ... from constituting an investment in a fractionalized mortgage, interest in a mortgage pool, tenancy in common or other security' ends with a broad 'or other security' catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the Co-Lending Activities permitted by 5.3(c) and 5.8 without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As written it is an affirmative covenant 'to make any mortgage loan, if ... aggregate principal of Portfolio Loans secured by real property located outside the United States ... exceeds twenty percent', which is the opposite of the evident intent — an apparent omitted negative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: So read it contradicts 3.7's statement that the Company lends on real property 'located primarily in the United States' and makes no sense as a covenant for the Noteholders' benefit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare covenant to perform; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It references the Subscription Agreement, Notes and Security Agreement consistently with 10.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Aggregate Principal balances exceeding fifty percent' is a definite threshold, with only a typographic slip in 'ageregate'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6's chapeau states a 'majority of the aggregate principal amounts' threshold for the same body of covenants, so two consent formulations govern overlapping ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite list of prohibited corporate events.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision authorises merger or dissolution, so the fit is clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Lien (as defined in the Security Agreement)' with an exception for what is 'permitted pursuant to the Security Agreement or this Agreement with respect to a Company Borrowing' leaves the exception's boundary uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.3(b) defines 'Lien' as the Noteholders' own security interest, so the same capitalised term bears a different meaning here, and 5.3(a) permits precisely the senior liens this clause forbids.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars direct salaries 'during any month in which a Portfolio Management Fee is payable', but no such term is defined anywhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.4(a) defines the fee as the 'Management Fee' (describing it as a monthly portfolio management fee), so the covenant's trigger term does not match the defined term it must refer to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A Member, including, without limitation, the Manager or their respective Affiliates (other than a Sponsored Investment Fund)' mixes a general class with enumerated specifics and a carve-out of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out again turns on 5.1(c)'s wide Sponsored Investment Fund definition, which elsewhere (5.7(b)(iv), 5.7(e)) also disapplies protective conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short prohibition; 'sole remaining Manager' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.3 contemplates 'manager or managers' collectively, which is consistent with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Materially and adversely effects' misuses 'effects' for 'affects', and 'economic interests of the Noteholders' is an imprecise measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble incorporates the Operating Agreement 'as it may be amended from time to time', which cuts against this restriction on amendments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Non-negotiable' plus an absolute consent requirement plus a further restriction to 'qualified investors only' (an undefined term) leaves the transfer regime layered and partly indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The securities legend permits transfer on an opinion of counsel without mentioning Company consent, and 1.7 and 8.1(b) contemplate assignments, so the transfer rules are not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (iii) says 'to comply with state or federal securities with respect to the issuance of the Notes', omitting the word 'laws', and 'may be appropriate under' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The power to execute 'amendments or cancellation' of this Agreement on a Noteholder's behalf is hard to reconcile with 1.5 and 10.5, which condition amendments on Noteholder consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Coupled with an interest' and 'irrevocable' are conventional, though the survival language is oddly limited to effecting a transfer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates a Noteholder delivering an assignment, while Section 7 makes any assignment without Company consent null and void.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or expedient' and 'necessary or appropriate in the judgment of the Manager' are broad but standard further-assurances formulations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly subordinate to 8.1 and parallels 4.2, so it coheres with the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actions of the Collateral Agent shall be binding on the Noteholders' combined with a first-priority claim on the Collateral for the agent's own fees is one-sided and its outer limits are unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 10.6, which preserves each Noteholder's cumulative remedies, and against 5.3(a)/9(b), under which the agent may be directed by the Manager to subordinate the Noteholders' security.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'On terms required by Manager' is a striking grant, limited only by what is 'not prohibited under this Agreement or the Security Agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lets the Manager direct the Noteholders' own agent to subordinate their Lien, which is in tension with 2.3(a)'s grant of security and 6.2(b)'s prohibition on liens.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The default-period consent requirement and the exclusion of affiliate-held Notes are stated with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'Majority in Interest' as defined in 6.2, consistently with 6.3 and 10.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as expressly provided in this Agreement' qualifies the no-third-party-beneficiary rule without identifying which provisions qualify.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9 (Collateral Agent) and 10.8-10.9 (Greenberg Traurig) confer benefits on non-parties, and Section 7 bars assignment though this clause binds 'successors and assigns'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional Delaware choice-of-law clause with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.8(d) measures counsel's conduct by the California Rules of Professional Conduct, a different body of law, though as a professional-conduct standard rather than a governing law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses execution formalities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear four-limb notice regime with definite deeming periods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.5 lets the Company waive 'any notice provision' in its discretion, which qualifies but does not contradict this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It combines a Majority in Interest requirement with a right for 'any Noteholder' to modify the Agreement as to his own Note and a Company right to waive notice and timing provisions, a layered scheme whose interaction is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 1.5 states a different amendment rule for the Notes (Company plus over-50% holders, with protection against discriminatory amendments), so two amendment regimes overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-waiver and cumulative-remedies language, clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9(a) makes the Collateral Agent's actions binding on Noteholders, which restricts the individual remedies this clause preserves as 'cumulative and not alternative'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional integration clause naming the constituent documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits the private placement memorandum relied on in 4.1(b) and the Operating Agreement incorporated by the preamble and 5.2, leaving the integrated set arguably incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but descriptive; a stray unclosed quotation mark around 'Company Counsel' and a mispunctuated 'Portfolio Transactions.)' are cosmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It addresses 'Each Investor' whereas the Agreement's defined parties are Purchasers and Noteholders, a terminological slip repeated in 5.7(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite disclaimer of representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.8(c) and 10.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as otherwise specifically provided by this Agreement' is an unspecified carve-out, but the substance is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision elsewhere requires the Company to pay Noteholder counsel, so the carve-out has no evident referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver covers only a 'present conflict of interest', while the consent extends to future disputes, a scope mismatch a court could be asked to resolve.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies the California Rules of Professional Conduct in an agreement governed by Delaware law under 10.2, and its protection interlocks with 10.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A consent to unrelated representations; the phrase 'matters of a similar nature to the Transactions' being 'unrelated' is somewhat self-contradictory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on 10.8 without conflicting with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Portfolio Loan Transaction' is used as though defined but is not, and the consent is conditioned at the end on a further specific consent, complicating its operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with 10.8(d) and 10.9(a) as part of the same conflicts-waiver scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense and repetitive ('with their permission' twice in one sentence), but the consent given is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10.8 and 10.9(a)-(b); no conflicting provision identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard restrictive legend whose conditions (registration statement or opinion of counsel) are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7 conditions any transfer on the Company's consent 'in its sole and absolute discretion' and limits transfers to 'qualified investors', which the legend does not mention, so the two transfer regimes do not match.
